notice: Prototype field mapping from the public Agentic Commerce OpenAPI document onto a partial KATA agreement. Cited keys are properties in that document. A verified status means the AmEx key was published, not that American Express defined the KATA placement. This file does not assert compatibility with American Express.

source.title: American Express Agentic Commerce Experience - Enrollment, Intent, Payment Credential, and Notification API (1.0.0)

input_schema_version.note: The OpenAPI document version is 1.0.0. Request schemas do not include schemaVersion. When a sender includes it, the value is kept. 1.0.0 matches the published document version and is still reported as assumed.

bindings.note: intentId is a required string on the create and update responses, and the path parameter on PUT and DELETE /payments/digital/v1/agentic-commerce/intents/{intentId}. It is not a property of IntentsRequest. agreement_id is the stable KATA record id.
The same intentId is copied onto the intent declaration so the intent object has an id. intent_id is not, by itself, the lifecycle key.
KATA mandate ids change when the signed version changes. The suffix is a draft stand-in. The source key intentId is the published identifier.

prompt.promptSummary is a required string: a summary of the purchase intent derived from user input. prompt.nlpConfidence is a separate number from 0 to 1 and is not this binding. Placing the summary on natural_language_source is assumed.

spendControl.maxAmount is a required string: the maximum amount that can be charged using the payment method. A plain decimal string is read as a major-unit number. The document does not publish a minor-unit scale. purchaseCriteria.maxAmount is a different field.
KATA restates the per-transaction ceiling on limits. This copy stays equal to maximum_amount only while both bindings read spendControl.maxAmount.

expirationTs on the intent is required, format date-time, described as the intent expiration in ISO 8601. spendControl.expirationTs is a different property, the payment-method expiration, and is not this binding.
The mandate end instant is the same intent expirationTs as intent.time_limit. When both KATA fields are set they are the same instant.

maxAllowedTransactions is an optional string: the maximum allowed transactions the user authorized to complete the purchase. KATA frequency.max_count counts recorded charges. requestedPaymentCredentialsCount on the payment-credential request is a different integer.

spendControl.currency is a required ISO 4217 string on the spend control. orderContext.currency, items[].currency, and purchaseCriteria.currency are separate properties. Using the spend-control currency as the intent currency is assumed.
The same spendControl.currency is copied onto limits.

orderContext.merchants[].name is published. The schema does not mark name required. merchantId is an integer. Placing names in merchant_constraints is assumed. categoryName is preserved and is not an allowlist entry.

purchaseCriteria lives on each item, not on orderContext. fromDate is date-time and is required when type is DATE. Writing the first item's first DATE criterion to not_before is assumed. type PRICE is not this binding.
toDate is date-time and is required when type is DATE. It fills expires_at only when intent expirationTs did not. The assignment is assumed.
The same toDate fills time_limit when intent expirationTs did not, so the two KATA end fields stay together.

scaffolds.note: Draft marker for an unsigned agreement. AmEx intentStatus is a different enum.
No charge has been recorded. The AmEx credential log is a different object.
Lifecycle events are not invented from the AmEx record.
First draft version. The OpenAPI update is PUT on the same intentId. This prototype does not build a new signed KATA version.
KATA requires an intent version. The OpenAPI document does not publish one.
The window is not published. agreement counts across the whole mandate window. KATA counts recorded charges. maxAllowedTransactions does not name a window.

kata_gaps.note: enrollmentId identifies the enrolled account. The intent user object carries firstName, lastName, a billing address, and email or phone plus PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes. Neither is a KATA principal, which needs a type, an id, and the signing public key.

IntentsRequest requires agent with agentName, llmPlatform, and llmVersion. The llmPlatform enum is OPEN_AI. The agentId header is required on these operations. KATA agent requires agent_id and a public-key fingerprint. Those AmEx fields are not that object.

proofOfIntent is a string on the intent response after step-up and on INTENT_UPDATE notifications. The description is a signed JSON Web Token. The schema does not publish claims or an algorithm. An example on the payment-credentials request uses a placeholder signature. No KATA JWS is produced.
KATA requires a purpose. The OpenAPI document has no purpose field.
No ledger sync time is present on the AmEx record.
